edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts point in more than one direction, so no single pooled effect estimate is reliable enough to summarize cleanly.
edges.mechanism: This exposure is studied mainly through oxidative stress, endocrine disruption, inflammatory signaling, or direct tissue toxicity, with the dominant pathway varying by pollutant. For Thyroid cancer, the main uncertainty is usually exposure measurement rather than complete biologic implausibility.
edges.summary: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts link drinking water nitrates to mixed effects on thyroid cancer in adults using contaminated groundwater. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: Exposure-based assessment and economic valuation of adverse birth outcomes and cancer risk due to nitrate in United States drinking water.
